title: improv·artist · industrial (Donald Judd)
mutation_directive: improv artist: industrial via Donald Judd

improv_extras.practice: stacked metal boxes; precise repetition; specificity of object

v1.feedback: The stacked structure and restrained metal palette reference Judd, but the circular particle flow within each slab undermines the core idea — Judd's work is about stillness, industrial weight, and specificity of object, not fluid dynamics. Particles should be densely packed to read as solid rectangular volumes with near-zero motion; consider using particle density and sharp cutoff edges to simulate material opacity rather than swirling dots. The wireframe boxes at 0.25 opacity are too ghostly to carry architectural weight — either make them crisper or let the particle density alone define the slab boundaries.

v2.feedback: Critical bug: slabId is stored normalized (0.0–0.9) in posData but the sim shader treats it as integer (0–9) in the yBase calculation, so on the very first sim step all slabs except slab-0 get clamped to wildly wrong y-positions and the stack collapses into a single crushed band. Fix by storing `s` not `s/SLABS` in the w channel (or multiply by 10.0 in the shader). If the bug were fixed the concept maps well to Judd — restrained aluminum palette, dense rectangular volumes, minimal motion — but consider giving the slabs slightly different surface treatment (anodized tint shift per slab, or subtle specular highlight gradient) so the repetition reads as deliberate specificity rather than copy-paste.
